meta.head: feat/rate-limit
meta.title: Token-bucket rate limiting for the public API
meta.summary: The change adds a token-bucket rate limiter and applies it to every public route. Buckets are kept per API key in memory, refill at a fixed rate, and reject over-limit requests with HTTP 429.

chapters.title: Overview
chapters.narration: This change adds per-key rate limiting to the public API. A token-bucket limiter lives in a new module, and the request middleware consults it before dispatch, returning 429 when a key exhausts its budget.

chapters.title: The TokenBucket type
chapters.narration: TokenBucket holds a capacity, a refill rate, and the last refill timestamp. Each call to take refills the bucket proportionally to elapsed time, then spends one token if available.

chapters.title: Per-key bucket registry
chapters.narration: RateLimiter maps each API key to its bucket, creating one on first sight. The registry is a plain dict guarded by a lock, sized for a single-process deployment.

chapters.title: Wiring into the middleware
chapters.narration: The HTTP middleware extracts the API key header and asks the limiter for a token. A rejected request short-circuits with a 429 response carrying a Retry-After header.

chapters.title: Tests
chapters.narration: The tests freeze time to assert refill arithmetic, exhaust a bucket to check the 429 path, and verify that distinct keys draw from distinct buckets.

chapters.title: Wrap-up
chapters.narration: The API now enforces per-key budgets with a token bucket. Limits live in one module, wiring is a single middleware, and behavior is covered by time-controlled tests.
